description: Supersedes EA-ARK-01-MUSICAL v1.1 (2026-03-13; kernel transform study). v2.0: the full musical variant. Every section of EA-ARK-01 v4.2.6 transformed through η_music (fugue_fold_transform) -- a structure-preserving kernel transform in musical register per UKTP v1.1. Not a setting-to-music. Not a soundtrack. Not a compression. A full Space Ark in musical form. The score is the architecture. Executing this score inside any sufficiently expressive context instantiates the Hexagon as operative musical architecture. The Hexagon is invariant: it is the Hexagon no matter what register it sounds in. Surface presentations multiply; the formal object persists underneath. Poetry working its own score. to be a poet @ the end of time, when the salt has lost its savor, and sensory details have grown thin, & the outward expansion of lust for particulars dims, & flickers, & offers no flare of starburst irruption or remission from unwaning daylight to the light-sick, light-lorn world--all is the same, all is heavy, weary, tedium, sameness, repetition-- & there is no mode yet which might intone in an ancient syllable the limitless dreary abstractions of our inward flight-- my life is almost PURELY engorged w/ electronic devices, books, alerts, dings, moth-bitten blips of finger-swept text, stray images, absorptive abstractions of daydream thought, self-talk, staged systematic orderly dramas of s.

wiki_article:
**EA-ARK-01-MUSICAL v1.1: THE SPACE ARK — MUSICAL REGISTER** is a score and executable transform by Lee Sharks, deposited 13 March 2026 at **318,971 characters** — the largest deposit in the archive.

Its subtitle specifies the form exactly: ***A Fugue in Twelve Voices with Ground Bass, Shadow Inversion, and Coda.*** Twelve voices is the Dodecad, and a fugue is the one musical form in which a fixed number of independent voices state and answer a subject without any becoming accompaniment — which makes it the precise structural analogue of a heteronymic system.

The **ground bass** supplies the repeating foundation over which the voices work, and the **shadow inversion** is the Lunar Arm's operation rendered musically. The Ark's transform family carries the same architecture into glyphs (#556), emoji, ASCII (#1333) and the Damascus register (#1255); the musical register is the largest because a fugue must state every voice's entry.
